title: From Enemies to Friends
summary: Because of our sin we were enemies of God. But those who surrender to Jesus are not just pardoned. God embraces them as friends.
exhortation: What does it mean to be reconciled, and why do we need it? Because of our sin, we are enemies of God. That's not a good position to be in. It's a losing position, to say the least. We were born rebels against God who hate the things of God. We hate being told what to do. We hate being told we are sinners who need to repent.

Maybe you feel that right now. Maybe you're watching and thinking, "What a foolish thing, to believe in a God who judges us for our sin and calls us enemies." But that doesn't change the fact that the God who created the ground you walk on, the air you breathe, the oceans and the stars, will punish sinners who rebel against his law. And we have all rebelled.

Wait, you say. I thought God was loving and kind. Yes, he is. He sent his only Son, Jesus, to pay the penalty for our sin and rebellion, so that whoever believes in him will not receive God's wrath but grace, reconciliation and forgiveness. Unless you put your trust in Jesus, you remain an enemy of God. But those who surrender their pride, their plans and their very lives will receive grace and mercy. They will no longer be called enemies. God will call them friends.

And know this: when you surrender, God doesn't gloat or rub your face in it. He quickly embraces you as part of his family and lifts you higher than you ever thought possible. So don't delay. Come to Jesus, and he will quickly forgive you and embrace you as a friend and a brother.
prayer: Lord, you are the Creator God, the maker of all things. As rebels and sinners opposed to your will, there was nothing we could have done to turn to you unless you intervened. All our hope is Christ. We have no leg to stand on.

What a great salvation and what a great hope we have in Jesus. If something in me had caused me to turn to you, I'd be terrified, because it would mean I could mess it up again. But all my hope, not part of it, is in you, Jesus, and you who began this work will finish it. Fix our eyes on you. Help us not lose the plot today, and keep this truth in our hearts: you are the rescuer who reached into the darkness and snatched us from the path to destruction we were on. Thank you, Lord. All glory be to your name.
